nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.whole: The credit was to rebuild housing and to put in evacuation shelters, evacuation routes and early warning systems in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry after the December 2004 tsunami. By the completion report's own count, 4,121 houses were finished to disaster-resistant standards, 29 per cent of the revised target of 14,370, and in Puducherry about 550 of the 1,752 houses taken into the project were finished. The same report records that no evacuation shelter was built against a revised target of 140, that no early warning system was installed against a revised target of 439, and that evacuation route works had not started when the credit closed. These figures are the lender's own; no independent count was found.
nagapattinam-canal-demolition-tsunami-re.searched: Cached completion report results framework (indicators 9, 12 and 14) and component sections, and the Independent Evaluation Group review.

ahwaz-jomhori-pumping-station-house-expr.whole: The loan paid for water and sewerage works in Ahwaz and Shiraz. In Ahwaz the completion report counts 79,853 new water connections and 99,175 new sewerage connections, and 131.1 km of water pipes rehabilitated against a target of 266 km. It reports 17 per cent of Ahwaz wastewater treated against a target of 50 per cent, with the treatment plants still under construction and the sewerage system not operational, and water unaccounted for in Ahwaz rising from 36.3 to 40 per cent. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
ahwaz-jomhori-pumping-station-house-expr.searched: Cached completion report (31 March 2010) results framework and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 22 September 2010.

iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.whole: The loan rehabilitated 320 km of Expressway 1 in southern Iraq and built 23 km of the Girsheen-Suheila section in the north. The completion report records travel time across the project roads falling from 4.0 hours to 2.72 hours, all project road segments classified as in good or fair condition at closing, and 109,825 people living near the roads counted as beneficiaries against a revised target of 90,000. It gives traffic fatalities on the project roads as 21 a year in its results table and as an average of 23 a year for 2020-2023 in its text, against 87 expected at appraisal. These figures are the lender's own; no independent count was found.
iraq-expressway-worker-deaths-vendor-rel.searched: Cached completion report (18 December 2023), paragraphs 25-33 and Table 4, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 2 May 2024.

jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.whole: The loan paid for street, facade and infrastructure works in Jerash, Karak, Salt, Ajloun and Madaba. The completion report gives average tourist stay in the project cities at 2.8 days against a target of 2.2 and a baseline of 1.5 days, property values in the target cities up 50 per cent against a 20 per cent target, and 697 direct and 306 indirect tourism jobs created against a target of 500, counted by an impact study the Bank and the Jordanian government commissioned. The Evaluation Group records that the planned Petra visitor centre was dropped from the project in 2011 and built instead with the government's own funds and a USAID grant. All of these figures come from the lender or the government.
jordan-heritage-cities-house-shop-demoli.searched: Cached completion report results tables (tables 12 and 13), paragraphs 58-60 and annex 3, and the Independent Evaluation Group review, outputs and efficiency sections.

tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.whole: The loan and its 2011 additional financing paid for street, facade and archaeological works in Baalbeck, Byblos, Saida, Tripoli and Tyre, and one completion report covers both. That report counts 274,000 square metres of pedestrian public space and 311,100 square metres of historic building facades rehabilitated, visitors to the five cities at 420,000 against a baseline of 203,000, and 1,575 people working in heritage and tourism businesses against a target of 1,500. The Evaluation Group records a 100 per cent cost overrun on the investments, the 2003 appraisal estimate of US$61.9 million rising to US$119.0 million. All of these figures come from the lender.
tripoli-tyre-heritage-market-relocation.searched: Cached completion report filed under the parent project P050529, which covers both P050529 and the P116197 additional financing, results tables; and the Independent Evaluation Group review, cost and efficiency sections.

lesotho-integrated-transport-farmland-an.whole: The credit and its later financing rehabilitated roads and built footbridges in Lesotho. The completion report records 40 km of the Oxbow-Mokhotlong road rehabilitated against a revised target of 40 km, three footbridges and access tracks built in the Senqu and Senqunyane area, and the 37 km Nyenye-Makhoroana road substantially complete at closing and finished in December 2015, the first 20 km with Bank money and the remaining 17 km with government money. It gives average travel cost in the targeted project areas down 40 per cent to 900 maloti a trip, and national roads at 38 per cent good against a target of 39 per cent and 50 per cent fair against a target of 46 per cent. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
lesotho-integrated-transport-farmland-an.searched: Cached completion report results framework (indicators 1, 2, 11, 13 and 14) and paragraph 27, and the Independent Evaluation Group review.

tabanovce-kumanovo-motorway-compensation.whole: The loan upgraded the 7.3 km Tabanovce to Kumanovo section to motorway standard, with two carriageways in each direction, and upgraded the passenger terminal at the Blace border crossing with Kosovo. The completion report gives waiting time at Blace falling from 10 to 2.5 minutes a vehicle on entry and from 12 to 1.9 minutes on exit, and the extra delay for freight trains at the Corridor X rail border removed, leaving the scheduled 90 minutes against 450 minutes before. Border crossing works stood at 97.6 per cent complete at closing, with 200 square metres of asphalting on an existing lane and a control cabin outstanding. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
tabanovce-kumanovo-motorway-compensation.searched: Cached completion report (12 December 2012) results framework, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 12 September 2013.

east-tsankhi-herder-displacement.whole: The credit and grant paid for technical work on Mongolia's mining sector, including the pre-feasibility study for the East Tsankhi coal mine. By the completion report's count, the Fiscal Stability Fund was being run by a department of the finance ministry under the Fiscal Stability Law of 2010, two mining tax audits were completed in 2014, one of which led to a tax dispute settled in the government's favour in 2015, and a computerised mining cadastre went online for licence applications. The same report records that the target of digitising 200,000 geological data points was not met, and that selected recommendations of the review of mining institutions were endorsed but no action plan to carry out the others was adopted. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
east-tsankhi-herder-displacement.searched: Cached completion report results framework (indicators 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6) and safeguards section, and the Independent Evaluation Group review.

beira-maputo-climate-works-deaths-compen.whole: The credit and climate funds paid for drainage works in Beira and Maputo and for land registers and revenue work in other municipalities. By the completion report's count, 667,219 people were given improved urban living conditions against a target of 418,000, 3,375 hectares in Beira and Maputo gained reduced flooding or erosion against a target of 1,140, 20 municipalities had a working land register against a target of 16, and 13 of 14 municipalities met their revenue targets. The same report notes that the indicator replaced an earlier one with a target of 2 million beneficiaries by 2017. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
beira-maputo-climate-works-deaths-compen.searched: Cached completion report (30 March 2021), paragraph 25 and Table 2, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 27 August 2021.

sena-railway-right-of-way-and-retrenchme.whole: The credit paid for rehabilitation of the 600 km Sena line from Dondo to Moatize, run under a private concession. The completion report records the first coal train leaving Moatize for Beira on 8 August 2011, the line finished two years later than expected, and freight and passenger traffic on it at 266,000 tonnes a year against a target of 1,000,000; it records no rehabilitation of the 317 km Machipanda line against a target of 317 km, leaving that line in worse condition than at the start, and traffic from Zimbabwe at 387,700 tonnes against a target of 650,000. Engineering News reported the rehabilitation about 18 months behind schedule, with completion then expected in November 2012, and the government cancelling the contract with the RITES and Ircon consortium after it did not deliver, with the state railway CFM asked to finish the work. The tonnage counts against target are the lender's own.
sena-railway-right-of-way-and-retrenchme.searched: Cached completion report results framework and the Evaluation Group review; Engineering News project page on the Sena line, which carries no publication date.

senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.whole: The credits and grants paid for irrigation works, dam studies and health measures in the Senegal River basin. The completion report counts 88 km of irrigation canals built or rehabilitated against a target of 50 km, 5,223 hectares of irrigated land rehabilitated or developed against a target of 4,400, 25 motor pumps installed and 22 pumping stations built or enlarged, and 534 hectares of lowland developed against a target of 900. Feasibility studies for three dams were completed, and on 25 March 2013 the heads of state of the river basin organisation decided to finance and build the Gouina and Koukoutamba dams. The Evaluation Group rated the quality of that completion report Unsatisfactory; the figures in it are the lender's own.
senegal-river-perimeter-crops-destroyed.searched: Cached completion report ICR2653 (25 September 2013) results framework, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 30 June 2015.

kamuzu-barrage-liwonde-businesses.whole: The credit and grants rebuilt the Kamuzu Barrage and paid for catchment and flood works in the Shire basin. By the completion report's count, the barrage's 14 gates were replaced and automated and the regulated level of Lake Malawi raised by 40 cm, a network of 100 weather and river monitoring stations was refitted, 35,385 hectares of catchment were rehabilitated, 27 per cent of the area targeted, and 3,155 households in flood-prone districts were reclassified to a lower flood risk against a revised target of 2,780. The report puts the number of people directly benefiting at 446,650 against a target of 400,000. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
kamuzu-barrage-liwonde-businesses.searched: Cached completion report paragraphs 28-35 and results annex, and the Evaluation Group review; a report in The Nation (Malawi) on the barrage's commissioning carried no publication date and gave cost figures it did not reconcile, so it was not used.

narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.whole: The credit upgraded the 33 km Narayanghat to Mugling section of the Birgunj-Kathmandu corridor to Asian Highway standard and built four bridges along it. The completion report records border crossing time at the Raxaul-Birgunj post falling from 2.30 days to 0.87 days, measured on 18,975 vehicles in August 2021, and the time from unloading cargo at Kolkata to reaching Kathmandu by truck falling from 10 days to 5.94 days. Slope stabilisation works at km 17 and km 26 were not finished within the project period and were completed afterwards by the government with its own money. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
narayanghat-mugling-road-structures.searched: Cached completion report (22 June 2022) results indicators and outputs annex, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 14 September 2022.

kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.whole: Component 1 was to build a 90 km 132 kV line and substations in eastern Nepal. The completion report records 34.5 km of line between Damak and Godak and three substations finished at closing, carrying 52 MW into the national system; the state utility then continued the work with its own resources, and by 31 August 2018 64 km of conductor was strung and 71 MW carried, against a target of 150 MW. It records the works contract at US$16.8 million against an estimate of US$31.563 million. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.
kabeli-transmission-line-compensation-ar.searched: Cached completion report (12 September 2018), paragraphs 19-20 and results framework, and the Independent Evaluation Group review of 14 January 2019.

pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.whole: The additional loan rebuilt roads damaged by the earthquake of 8 October 2005. The completion report for the parent highways project records 128 km reconstructed or rehabilitated and reopened to traffic: 44 km of the N-15 between Basian, Balakot, Mahindri and Naran, 25 km of the N-35 between Battal, Batgram and Thakot, and 59 km of the Jhelum Valley Road. The Evaluation Group puts the whole operation's cost at US$576 million against US$361 million at the start, and re-estimates its economic rate of return at 26 per cent against 33 per cent at appraisal, noting localised distress and an early need for repairs. Both accounts come from the lender.
pakistan-earthquake-roads-compensation-a.searched: Cached completion report for the parent project P010556, whose documents the Bank files under the same Highways Rehabilitation Project as P099040, component tables and cost annex; and the Independent Evaluation Group review.

peru-rural-electrification-right-of-way-.whole: The loan subsidised rural grid extensions and solar home systems run by public electricity distribution companies. The Evaluation Group's assessment report counts infrastructure for 105,000 grid connections installed, serving about 450,000 people and including around 2,900 schools, clinics and community centres, and regulated service for 7,100 households on solar systems. It puts new connections 34 per cent below the original target of 160,000, with average cost per connection at US$1,100 against the US$715 estimated during preparation, and rural electricity coverage up 5.9 per cent. All of these figures come from the lender's own evaluation office.
peru-rural-electrification-right-of-way-.searched: Cached Project Performance Assessment Report (30 June 2017), chapter 4, with the completion report of 26 December 2013 and the Evaluation Group review of 17 June 2015.

manila-sewerage-site-clearances-san-mate.whole: The loan paid for sewage and septage treatment plants and septic tank emptying in the east zone of Metro Manila. The Evaluation Group's review counts six of the nine plants planned after restructuring completed, of which three were operational at closing, 262,012 septic tanks emptied against a target of 250,560, and 77,137 water connections given sewerage treatment service, 66 per cent of the original target of 117,000 and 56 per cent above the reduced target of 49,000 set at the January 2011 restructuring. It gives pollutant removal attributable to the project at 1,415 tonnes a year in 2012 against a target of 20,400, and 11,499 cubic metres of sewage treated between 2010 and 2012 against an original target of 113,227. The completion report puts the number of plants treating flows in compliance with discharge standards at six against a target of eight and records that indicator as not achieved, with the plants running below capacity; all of these figures come from the lender.
manila-sewerage-site-clearances-san-mate.searched: Cached completion report results framework (indicator 4) and the paragraph on the discharge-standards indicator, and the Independent Evaluation Group review, outputs and outcomes sections.

dennery-embankment-land-used-without-com.whole: The works defended Dennery village from the sea and the river. A Government of Saint Lucia notice of 7 February 2005 set out the two phases to be paid for with US$7.5 million from the World Bank: a 415-metre buried revetment between the waterfront and High Street, three offshore breakwaters of 50, 50 and 60 metres, an armoured berm with landfill behind it, and a 50-metre revetment on the village's north boundary. A Bank land acquisition report of 20 February 2007 records those coastal protection works as finished in the first week of September 2006 at a contract price of 6,683,042.53 East Caribbean dollars, and a second contract for the Dennery River and ravine works, at 1,429,505.77 East Caribbean dollars, as still under way and scheduled to finish in July 2007. Both accounts come from the lender and the government; no independent check was found.
dennery-embankment-land-used-without-com.searched: Cached land acquisition and resettlement report of 20 February 2007 (the only Bank document on disk for this number); Government of Saint Lucia press notice of 7 February 2005; web search for a completion report, an audit or press coverage of the Dennery sea defences found none, only later unrelated drainage works under a 2019-2021 project.

sources_add.title: US $7.5 Million for Dennery Waterfront Protection Project

chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.whole: The credit paid for an inland container depot in the Kathmandu valley. The Kathmandu Post puts the depot at Chobhar, on 11.77 hectares, built for Rs1.54 billion with a World Bank loan, with room for 500 containers and 500 trucks and an export-import section of 116 twenty-foot equivalent units. The completion report says the depot was substantially complete when the project closed in November 2021 and in operation from April 2022. The Kathmandu Post reported in June 2022 that fewer than two dozen container trucks had arrived since it opened, and in November 2023 that Chobhar customs recorded imports of Rs642.30 million and exports of Rs14.42 million in the last fiscal year, and imports of Rs389.61 million, up 148.34 per cent on the same period a year earlier, with no exports in the first four months of the current one.
chobhar-dry-port-arrests-kathmandu.searched: Cached completion report and Evaluation Group review for the project, neither of which names Chobhar; two Kathmandu Post reports on the depot's use and on the lease to a private operator.

Government ropes in private sector to operate Chobhar dry port
